lateral_torso_line_topology.vertical_line_count_and_spacing: Approximately 11 distinct vertical white lines are visible on the lateral torso. Spacing is approximately 50-70 pixels between lines in the central ribcage area, becoming tighter and less defined towards the posterior.
lateral_torso_line_topology.intersection_coordinates_bifurcations: A Y-shaped bifurcation is visible on the third vertical line from the anterior edge, splitting approximately 1/4 of the way down from the dorsal mane.
lateral_torso_line_topology.discontinuity_mapping: The 10th and 11th posterior lines are abbreviated, terminating mid-flank and not extending to the ventral fringe.

posterior_constellation_clusters.spatial_cluster_density: A cluster of 5 high-contrast white spots is visible on the mid-to-lower haunch area, arranged in a semi-triangular formation.
posterior_constellation_clusters.linear_blob_alignment: Two distinct white spots on the upper hind limb align horizontally, parallel to the ventral line.

macro_horn_vector_geometry.curve_trajectory_2d: The primary visible horn exhibits a lyrate spiral trajectory, initiating at a roughly 60-degree angle from the frontal bone before curving posteriorly and then vertically.
macro_horn_vector_geometry.terminal_contrast_ratio: The high-contrast ivory tip constitutes approximately 12% of the total visible linear length of the horn structure.

other_distinctive_markers: Three visible Red-billed Oxpeckers (Buphagus erythrorhynchus) are present on the specimen: one on the upper neck below the ear, one on the ventral fringe, and one on the lower hind leg.
